Teenagers Free Time

Grade 9 · Unit 2 · Lesson 5 · Interactive English Lesson

“Free time is the enemy of progress.” — Casey Neistat

Learning Objectives

To discuss how teenagers spend their free time and justify opinions.
To identify and interpret key facts from an authentic-style reading text.
To use emphatic pronouns and phrasal verbs correctly.
To plan and present a school extracurricular magazine.
🔊 Voice Settings · Choose an English voice

Uses English voices installed in your browser or operating system. If no voice is available, install an English speech voice in Windows or try Edge. Audio is not guaranteed on every device.

Warm-up · Think, Pair, Share

Would you prefer one extra hour of free time or one extra hour of sleep? Give one reason. Discuss with a partner (60 seconds).

Speaking · Exercises 1–3

1How do you spend your free time? What activities do you prefer? How about your friends?
Model answerI enjoy reading, listening to music and meeting my friends. My friends prefer playing sports and watching films. We sometimes go for walks together.
2Read the quotes and say whether you agree or disagree.
Your success will be in direct proportion to how you spend your free time.
I had so much free time that free time was meaningless.
Free time is a terrible thing to waste. Read a book.

Choose one quotation. Explain your opinion and give an example.

3Complete the sentences using the words from the textbook.

leisure time · record time · free time · precious time · spare time

Reading · Exercise 4

Read the article. Find out how teenagers enjoy their free time. Make a mind map of the main ideas.

Click any word to see its contextual translation and hear its pronunciation. Words not in the glossary are marked as translation unavailable, rather than given an invented meaning.

Mind Map · Think first, then compare

Write one important fact from the article in each box. Then press Check / Compare to see possible answers. Different correct ideas are welcome.

Writing · Exercise 15 · Extracurricular Magazine

Work in teams. Design a magazine about extracurricular activities in your community. Give details about activities teenagers can practise in their free time.

Show complete model magazine

TEEN LIFE — Discover Your Talents!

For: Students aged 13–16

Robotics Club: Meet every Tuesday after school. Build simple robots, learn coding and work in teams. No previous experience is required.

Drama Club: Meet every Thursday. Practise acting, improve pronunciation and gain confidence when speaking in public.

Why join? Extracurricular activities help teenagers make friends, discover interests and develop useful skills for future careers.

Our message: Try something new this month!
